content: Childhood vaccinations should ideally be administered prior to initiating myeloablative conditioning. The safety and effectiveness of vaccinations during or after treatment with atidarsagene autotemcel have not been studied. Vaccinations are not recommended during the six weeks preceding the start of myeloablative conditioning and should be avoided until hematologic recovery is achieved following treatment. If feasible, all childhood vaccinations should be completed before starting myeloablative conditioning. Certain vaccines, such as the pneumococcal vaccine (21-valent and polyvalent), poliovirus vaccine (inactivated), rabies vaccine (including chick embryo cell-derived), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines (adjuvanted or mRNA), rotavirus oral vaccine (live), smallpox and monkeypox vaccines (live, non-replicating), typhoid vaccines (polysaccharide or live), varicella virus vaccine (live), yellow fever vaccine, and zoster vaccines (live or recombinant), are not recommended during this period. The safety of these vaccines in the context of atidarsagene autotemcel treatment has not been established. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, such as raltegravir, rilpivirine, ritonavir, tenofovir DF, tipranavir, zidovudine, abacavir, bictegravir, cabotegravir, efavirenz, elvitegravir, emtricitabine, enfuvirtide, etravirine, and fosamprenavir, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. These medications should not be taken for at least one month before cell mobilization or for the expected duration required for their elimination. Vaccines for diseases such as anthrax (adjuvanted or adsorbed), chikungunya (live), cholera, COVID-19 (adjuvanted or mRNA-based), dengue, Ebola Zaire, Haemophilus influenzae type b, hepatitis A, hepatitis B, hepatitis A/B combination, human papillomavirus (nonavalent), influenza A (H5N1), and others should also be avoided during the six weeks before myeloablative conditioning and until hematologic recovery is complete. The safety and efficacy of these vaccines in the context of atidarsagene autotemcel treatment remain unstudied. In summary, it is critical to complete all necessary childhood vaccinations before starting myeloablative conditioning whenever possible.
